who: Andrew Wender Cohen, historian of United States law and political economy at Syracuse University; PhD Chicago 1999.

evidence.says: Identifies Andrew Wender Cohen as a Syracuse history professor, with a Chicago history PhD in 1999 and Syracuse appointments beginning in 1999.
Authority for Andrew Wender Cohen cites The Racketeer's Progress and identifies him with Syracuse University in the record for Gangster of New York.

notes: The authority, institution, appointment period and exact doctorate institution/year agree.

who: Clifford M. Foust, historian at the University of Maryland, College Park; PhD history, Chicago 1957.

evidence.says: Faculty listing identifies Clifford M. Foust as professor emeritus of history, with Chicago MA 1951 and PhD 1957.
Washington Post obituary states that Foust earned his history doctorate at Chicago, began teaching at Maryland in 1970 and retired in 1995.
Authority for Clifford M. Foust cites Rhubarb and describes a history doctorate from Chicago and a professorship in Maryland's history department at College Park.

notes: Exact doctorate year agrees; Maryland appointment covers the listed students' 1973–1995 dates.

who: John B. Frantz, historian of Pennsylvania and colonial America at Penn State; PhD University of Pennsylvania.

evidence.says: Pennsylvania Historical Association biography identifies his Pennsylvania MA and PhD and Penn State history faculty service from 1961 to 1998; lists Pennsylvania's Religious Leaders among his works.
Authority for John B. Frantz cites Pennsylvania Religious Leaders and Penn State files identifying him as a history professor emeritus.

notes: Authority and scholarly-society biography identify the same Penn State historian; faculty dates cover all listed students. The biography prints the PhD year as '961', an apparent typographical omission.

who: Carl V. Harris, historian of United States urban politics and the South at UC Santa Barbara; PhD Wisconsin–Madison.

evidence.says: Department memorial states that Harris joined UCSB history in 1968 and retired in 2011; identifies Political Power in Birmingham, 1871–1921 as his book.
Authority for Carl V. Harris identifies the UCSB history department through Santa Barbara Presidio Area and reports a Wisconsin–Madison PhD in 1968 and over forty years teaching history at UCSB.

notes: Institution, field and career identify the candidate. LC reports PhD 1968, whereas own_phd gives 1970; retain this date discrepancy. Later listed student dates extend beyond the department's retirement date and were not individually verified.

who: Emily M. Hill, historian of modern China at Queen's University; PhD Cornell 1996.

evidence.says: Department profile identifies Emily M. Hill, associate professor, with a Cornell PhD in 1996 in modern Chinese history; lists Smokeless Sugar.
Authority for Emily M. Hill cites Smokeless Sugar and identifies its author as associate professor of history at Queen's University.
Bingru Yue's From Wetland Wilderness to Ecological Model explicitly thanks supervisor Professor Emily Hill and describes being her doctoral student.

notes: Exact doctorate institution/year, faculty identity and a listed student's acknowledgement agree.

who: Sheyda F. A. Jahanbani, historian of US foreign relations and global history at the University of Kansas; PhD history, Brown.

evidence.says: Kansas history profile identifies her field, Brown history doctorate and book The Poverty of the World.
Authority for Sheyda F. A. Jahanbani cites The Poverty of the World and an Oxford University Press biography identifying her as a Kansas history associate professor.
Kansas news identifies Jahanbani as a history associate professor who has been at KU since 2007.
Brown lists Jahanbani's dissertation, A Different Kind of People: The Poor at Home and Abroad, 1935–1980, under PhDs awarded in 2008–2009.

notes: Name, book, institution, field and doctorate school agree. Brown's award list places her in 2008–2009, whereas own_phd gives 2007; the year discrepancy remains unresolved.

who: Richard Joseph Lemay, historian of medieval science and astrology at CUNY's Graduate School; PhD history, Columbia 1958.

evidence.says: University of South Carolina Libraries finding aid identifies Richard Joseph Lemay, Columbia history PhD 1958, CUNY Graduate School associate professor 1970–1975, professor 1975–1986 and emeritus 1986–1989.

Charles Burnett's scholarly obituary identifies the historian of medieval astrology, his Columbia thesis under Lynn Thorndike and professorship at City College and CUNY's Graduate School in 1970–1986.
Authority for Richard Joseph Lemay identifies Richard Lemay as holding a Columbia PhD and cites his work on Pomponazzi.

notes: Full name, exact doctorate institution/year, CUNY appointment and medieval-science field agree with the supervisor and student topics.

who: Raymond Curtis Miller, historian at Wayne State University; PhD Chicago 1928, dissertation on the Populist Party in Kansas.

evidence.says: Authority identifies Raymond Curtis Miller through the 1928 thesis The Populist Party in Kansas and describes the author of Kilowatts at Work as Wayne State's history professor.
Chicago alumni magazine reports that Raymond Curtis Miller completed The Populist Party in Kansas among the June graduates and was teaching history at the College of the City of Detroit.
Wayne State University Archives identifies history professor Raymond C. Miller as co-chair of its Centennial Commission, documented in records for 1964–1968.
The separate economist Raymond C. Miller authority cites International Political Economy and specifies a Syracuse PhD and Chicago MA.

notes: The Wayne State historian matches the doctorate, dissertation and student period. Reject economist n2007088894: his Chicago degree is an MA and his PhD is from Syracuse.
